chunks: Tafsir al-Ayyashi: From Safwan who said:
I asked Aba al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the words of Allah: 'so wash your faces and your hands with the elbows and wipe part of your head and feet to the ankles'
He said: A man asked Aba al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about that, so he said: 'Surat al-Maida is enough for you' – meaning – wiping the head and the two feet…

key_terms.الْكَعْبَيْنِ: The ankles (in the context of feet)
key_terms.الْمَرَافِقِ: Elbows (in the context of washing hands)
key_terms.سُورَةُ الْمَائِدَةِ: Surah Al-Maida (the fifth chapter of the Quran)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia interpretation of wiping versus washing feet in the verse of purification?
ai.summary: This narration from Tafsir al-Ayyashi highlights Imam al-Rida’s (AS) concise method of interpreting Ayat al-Taharah by pointing to Surah al-Ma'idah as self-sufficient for establishing the ruling of wiping the feet (Masah) rather than washing them. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential stance that the verse's mention of 'feet' implies wiping, a view supported by the broader context of the Surah and contrasting with the Sunni practice of washing. The reference to a prior similar inquiry illustrates the consistency of the Imams' teachings on this fundamental ritual purification.
